Insufficient Transport Layer Security [Spoofing, Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-319] on CloudFront, APIGateway, LoadBalancer, BiddingService, AdService: Without proper TLS configuration and certificate management, communications between various components could be vulnerable to interception and modification. An attacker could perform a man-in-the-middle attack to intercept bid requests, modify bid amounts, or steal sensitive advertiser information.

Insufficient Authentication and Authorization [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-287] on APIGateway, IAM, WAF, BiddingService, campaign_db: The current implementation relies on API keys and IAM roles but lacks proper user authentication and session management. WAF protection is inconsistent across different user types. An attacker could steal API keys or exploit the lack of proper session management to impersonate advertisers or bypass spending limits.

Cache Inconsistency and Data Race Conditions [Tampering, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, CWE-664] on bid_cache, bid_store, BiddingService, bid_processors: Cache inconsistencies can occur due to race conditions during concurrent updates or failed write-through operations to the primary data store. An attacker could exploit timing windows between cache and database updates to manipulate bid data or cause financial inconsistencies.

Insufficient Data Privacy in Analytics Pipeline [Information Disclosure, CWE-359] on event_stream, analytics, data_lake, analytics_cluster: Sensitive user and bid data flows through multiple analytics components without proper anonymization or access controls, potentially exposing PII or business-sensitive information. An attacker with access to the analytics pipeline or data lake could extract sensitive user information or competitive bidding data.

Denial of Service Through Bid Request Flooding [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on CloudFront, APIGateway, WAF, bid_handlers, BiddingService: The system could be overwhelmed by a high volume of bid requests, either malicious or due to misconfigured clients, leading to service degradation. An attacker could flood the system with bid requests to overwhelm resources or cause processing delays that affect legitimate bids.

Insecure Direct Object References in Campaign Management [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-639] on APIGateway, campaign_db, CampaignMgmtLambda: Campaign management endpoints might not properly validate object ownership and access rights, allowing unauthorized access to or modification of campaign data. An attacker could modify campaign IDs or reference parameters to access or modify campaigns belonging to other advertisers.
